draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Pala! This town on the Meenachil River is a major hub of Syrian Christian culture, and it's surrounded by rubber plantations, rivers and hills.
draft.hungryLine: Pala eats Syrian Christian style. Try drum-cut tapioca with green chilli, onion and coconut oil, or mashed jackfruit with beef curry.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The tall granite Shrine of St. Mary is right in the heart of town. Kadappattur Temple is about 1.5 km away on the Meenachil.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head down to the Meenachil River for a quiet hour, or watch rubber being tapped on a plantation nearby.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Shrine of St. Mary has a massive statue of Jesus Christ on top. Wikivoyage compares it to the one in Rio de Janeiro, size aside.

spots.name: Shrine of St. Mary
spots.detail: In the heart of town · Tall granite shrine with a huge statue

spots.name: Kadappattur Temple
spots.detail: 1.5 km away · Shiva temple on the Meenachil

spots.name: Bharananganam Church
spots.detail: Pilgrim church · Where St. Alphonsa's mortal remains are kept

legends.title: The day the idol appeared
legends.body: Every year on 14 July, people celebrate the birthday of Kadappatturappan. It's said that's the day the idol appeared.

legends.title: The famous toddy shop
legends.body: Panthathala is a rubber-farming village on the Meenachil near Pala. Its toddy shop was famous in the 1980s and 90s, back when pre-degree courses were the norm.

tips.title: Come in early December.
tips.body: The feast of St. Mary, Pala's biggest festival, falls in the first week of December, and Pala Jubilee is on 7 December.

tips.title: Be careful with toddy.
tips.body: Good palm toddy can't be guaranteed unless it comes straight from the tree, and spurious additives are not uncommon.

story.title: Old churches
story.body: Lalam Old Church is one of the oldest churches in the region. Pala grew into a major hub of Syrian Christian culture in Kerala.

story.title: Rubber town
story.body: Pala became a plantation town, deeply tied to natural rubber. Villages around it, like Panthathala, still live mostly by rubber farming.

story.title: A small busy town
story.body: The 2011 census counted 22,056 people in Pala. It's also the headquarters of Meenachil Taluk.

story.title: Pilgrims and feasts
story.body: Pilgrims come for St. Alphonsa at Bharananganam and stop at Kadappattur on the way to Sabarimala. December brings the feast of St. Mary and Pala Jubilee.

food.name: Coffee and Snacks
food.detail: Near Kurishupally · Cutlet, vellayappam, dosa and beef fry

food.name: Ann's Bake House
food.detail: Short eats, cakes and pastries, cheaper than in the big cities
